transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm seeking help because I've been struggling with a very deep depression for over a year now. But recently, over the last few months, I've also been experiencing intense mood swings and periods of being unusually energetic and wired. It has become really difficult to manage on my own.
Can you tell me more about these periods of being unusually energetic and wired, such as how long they last and whether you've had any episodes that lasted for several days or longer?
During those times, I have this overflowing energy where I feel constantly wired and literally cannot sit still. This hyperactive state went on continuously for about four months.
Did you experience any psychotic symptoms, such as hallucinations or delusions, or required hospitalization during those four months when you felt constantly wired and hyperactive?

No, I didn't experience any hallucinations or delusions, and I didn't need to be hospitalized. Even though I was incredibly energetic, hyperactive, and made some really impulsive decisions, I never lost touch with reality.

Did these periods of high energy and impulsivity significantly impair your social or occupational functioning, or were you still able to maintain your daily life and responsibilities despite feeling wired and hyperactive?

Although I felt highly productive and full of energy, my actions actually caused some really significant problems. I ended up making reckless business investments without properly reviewing them and went on unrestrained shopping sprees that caused severe financial distress for me and my family.

During those four months of high energy and impulsivity, did you ever feel that your mood shifted to an extremely elevated or irritable state, where you might have appeared abnormally happy or angry to others, to the point of causing marked impairment in social or occupational functioning?

Yes, my mood shifted unpredictably during those four months. I would feel abnormally happy, euphoric, and full of energy, but then suddenly become extremely irritable and angry over the smallest things. People around me definitely noticed these extreme shifts, and it caused a lot of tension.

Can you estimate how many days out of those four months you spent in this extremely elevated or irritable state, and did you require any intervention or support from others to manage your behavior during that time?

I'm not sure of the exact number of days, but it felt like it was ongoing for almost the entire four months. I didn't require any professional intervention or hospitalization, though my family definitely had to step in to try and manage the financial mess I was making.

You mentioned earlier that you didn't experience hallucinations or delusions during the four months of high energy and impulsivity, but I want to confirm: are you certain you didn't have any episodes where you heard voices, saw things that weren't there, or had firmly held beliefs that weren't based in reality?

Yes, I am absolutely certain about that. I never heard any voices, saw things that weren't there, or believed in things that weren't real. My mind was racing and I made poor choices, but I always remained fully aware of reality.

Is there anything else you'd like to share about your symptoms, medical history, or any other factors that you think might be relevant to understanding what you're experiencing and how we can best help you?

I really want to understand these extreme shifts, as I've been deeply depressed, feeling worthless, and having thoughts of death for over a year now. Yet, I also had that distinct four-month period of being the complete opposite—overflowing with energy, constantly active, and making reckless financial decisions. It is incredibly exhausting to live between these two extremes.

Just to confirm once more, and to make sure we haven't missed anything, you're certain that during any of your episodes of extreme energy, irritability, or depression, you never experienced any break from reality, such as hearing voices, seeing things that aren't there, or having beliefs that aren't based in reality?

While I've never seen or heard things that aren't there, I did have some beliefs during my depression that felt disconnected from reality. I experienced an intense, completely unrealistic sense of guilt, feeling like I was somehow responsible for bad things happening around me that had absolutely nothing to do with me.
Can you elaborate on what you mean by an 'intense, completely unrealistic sense of guilt' during your depressive episodes, and how that affected your thoughts and behaviors?

During my low periods, I constantly replay minor mistakes from my past in my head and feel an overwhelming, irrational sense of blame for everyday negative events. It gets so extreme that I sometimes feel deeply responsible for tragic things happening to other people or even in the world, even though they have absolutely nothing to do with me.
